The accused, Ng Sui-ting, appeared in court this morning wearing a green Polo shirt, beige shorts and a black mask. The charges allege that on 10 July and 17 August, the accused allowed a male yellow mixed-breed dog to enter the vicinity of Yuen Long YOHO Mall without being restrained by a leash no longer than two metres, and faces two counts of "permitting a large dog to enter or remain in a public place".

The prosecution applied for the case to be adjourned for ten weeks for further mention and did not oppose bail. Acting Principal Magistrate Tang Siu-hung agreed to adjourn the case to 29 October for mention, and the accused was granted bail.

According to the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, a conviction for "permitting a large dog to enter or remain in a public place" carries a fine of HK$25,000 and three months' imprisonment.

Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, Yip Yin, said yesterday that if the dog owner decides to hand over the large dog to the government, the department will consider methods including humane treatment; if the owner intends to take the dog back, the dog may be classified as a "known dangerous dog", and the court may order that it must wear a muzzle whenever it goes out in future.

Kent, founder of animal protection organisation Mong Save Rescue, told Collective Journalism that the dog owner regrets signing the abandonment letter; he also said Mong Save is willing to take in the dog and provide a dog trainer for rehabilitation.
